title: Registration data can be linked to an existing identity
description: The registration flow sends strong identifiers and quasi-identifiers together (email, full name, government ID, and a six-digit code) from the parent to the authentication service. This enables the service, or any party that gains access to the flow, to link the new account registration to an already known real-world identity and potentially to other accounts or records.
assumptions: The authentication service can observe and store all submitted fields together and may have access to other internal or external identity datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode for linkability of multiple identifiers in one message may vary.

title: Parent identity is directly identifiable from registration payload
description: The flow contains direct identifiers such as name, email address, and government ID. Anyone with access to the message can immediately identify the parent without needing additional auxiliary data.
assumptions: The payload is available in clear to the authentication service and possibly intermediate components such as logs, monitoring, or proxies.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for direct identifiability from communicated content.

title: Excessive personal data disclosure during account creation
description: Highly sensitive registration attributes are disclosed in a single flow, including government ID and credentials. If the collection is broader than strictly necessary for authentication, the flow creates unnecessary disclosure of personal data to the authentication service and to any component that processes or logs the request.
assumptions: Not all fields may be strictly necessary at initial authentication-service intake; the service or surrounding infrastructure may log request bodies.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data disclosure via oversharing/overcollection in a data flow.

title: Sensitive credentials and identifiers may be exposed in transit or logs
description: The flow includes a password, government ID, email, and verification code. If transport protection, request-body redaction, or secure logging are insufficient, these values could be exposed to network observers, reverse proxies, application logs, or support tooling.
assumptions: Possible logging, tracing, or interception points exist between the external entity and the authentication service.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best match for disclosure through communication/intermediate observation; exact subnode may differ.

title: Parent may be unaware of full sensitivity and downstream use of submitted data
description: The parent may not understand why a government ID and six-digit code are required during registration, how long these data will be retained, or whether they will be reused for verification, fraud checks, or account recovery. This creates a risk that data subjects are insufficiently informed about collection and processing.
assumptions: The flow itself does not guarantee contextual notice, just-in-time explanation, or layered privacy information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency arising at data collection time.

title: Collection of government ID may be non-compliant if not necessary or properly justified
description: Requesting a government ID in a basic registration flow may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or lawful-basis requirements if the service cannot justify why this identifier is needed at this stage. The flow therefore raises non-compliance risk tied to unnecessary or disproportionate collection.
assumptions: Applicable privacy regulation requires necessity, proportionality, and transparency for collection of official identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed estimate for non-compliance due to excessive collection/purpose issues.

title: Lack of verifiable evidence of notice and consent for sensitive registration data
description: If the parent later disputes having provided the government ID or accepted the privacy terms associated with registration, the flow may not produce privacy-relevant proof of what was presented and agreed to at submission time. This creates a non-repudiation gap around privacy notices and permissions rather than around generic transaction integrity.
assumptions: No separate auditable record of consent/notice acknowledgment is created alongside the registration submission.
uncertainty_note: This threat is more context-dependent than the others; included as a possible privacy non-repudiation issue, and the exact node id may differ.

title: Stored parent account records can enable linkage across sessions, children, and household members
description: Persisting parent account data in the users collection can create a stable identifier set that allows records from different sessions or related family accounts to be linked together, revealing relationship patterns and long-term behavior.
assumptions: The parent account contains persistent identifiers such as email address, phone number, device references, or family/account relationship identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability from stored identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Parent account storage may permit identification of the parent
description: Storing direct or quasi-identifiers in the users collection, such as name, email, phone number, address, or payment-related metadata, can allow the parent to be directly identified from the stored record.
assumptions: The stored parent account includes direct identifiers or a combination of attributes sufficient to single out the individual.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability via stored data.

title: Stored parent account data may expose sensitive personal information
description: The users collection may contain personal details about the parent account holder, such as contact information, child/guardian relationships, preferences, or security metadata. If stored in excessive detail or insufficiently protected, these data may disclose private facts.
assumptions: The account record includes more than minimal authentication state and may include profile or family-relationship information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for information disclosure from data at rest; exact subtree may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Storing full parent account records without minimization creates unnecessary data exposure
description: If the authentication service writes more parent account attributes than are necessary for authentication and account management, the datastore accumulates excessive personal data, increasing privacy impact and downstream exposure.
assumptions: The flow may store full account/profile objects rather than a minimized schema limited to required fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization/aggregation concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Parents may be unaware of what account data are stored in the users collection
description: When account details are persisted internally by the authentication service, the parent may lack visibility into which attributes, relationship data, and retention periods apply, leading to insufficient user awareness about processing.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate all stored fields, purposes, and retention rules at account creation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of user awareness/transparency tied to storage; exact node id may vary.

title: Storing parent account data without a defined purpose or retention basis risks non-compliance
description: If the users collection stores parent account information without clear purpose limitation, retention limits, or lawful-basis handling, the processing may violate privacy obligations and internal policies.
assumptions: Applicable compliance requirements impose purpose limitation, retention control, and transparency obligations on account data storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node estimate; exact LINDDUN Pro node id is uncertain.

title: Excessive disclosure of user attributes in authentication response
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the response includes more personal data than is necessary for the parent-facing task (for example full profile details, internal identifiers, child-related metadata, or account status fields), the flow discloses personal information beyond the minimum needed.
assumptions: Assumes the parent only needs a subset of the user data to complete sign-in or establish session context.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for unnecessary or excessive personal-data disclosure in a data flow.

title: JWT enables cross-context linkability of parent activity
description: If the JWT contains stable identifiers or reusable claims (such as persistent subject IDs, email address, account number, or device-correlatable claims), the parent user's interactions across sessions, services, or relying components may become linkable. This can allow profiling of the same individual over time or across contexts.
assumptions: Assumes the token is reused across requests or accepted by multiple components, and that it contains persistent identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for linkability caused by persistent identifiers in authentication tokens.

title: JWT and user data can reveal parent identity
description: The flow may directly identify the parent user if the JWT payload or accompanying user data contains identifying attributes such as name, email, phone number, account ID, or other unique identifiers. Even if encoded, JWT claims are commonly readable by the recipient and potentially others with access to the token.
assumptions: Assumes the token/user payload includes direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is a best-fit estimate for identifiability through direct identifiers in flow contents.

title: Insufficient user awareness of personal data contained in login response
description: The parent user may not be aware that, beyond authentication, the response includes additional user data and readable JWT claims. If the system does not clearly communicate what data is returned and how it is used or stored on the client side, the user may be unable to make informed privacy decisions.
assumptions: Assumes there is limited notice or transparency about response contents and downstream token handling.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for lack of awareness/transparency regarding data disclosed in this flow.

title: Lack of meaningful choice over receipt and reuse of authentication-related user data
description: The parent user may be forced to accept receipt of a JWT bundled with user data as a condition of authentication, without granular control over optional profile data returned or subsequent reuse of those data on the client side. This can undermine consent or user choice regarding personal-data processing.
assumptions: Assumes some returned user attributes are optional for authentication and that no granular controls are offered.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for non-compliance or invalid-consent risk due to absent choice in the flow.

title: Parent may be unable to prove or contest what personal data were disclosed at login
description: If the system does not provide adequate records or receipts of the exact JWT claims and user data disclosed to the parent during authentication, the individual may be unable to later demonstrate what information was shared, challenge inaccuracies, or support privacy complaints.
assumptions: Assumes no user-accessible logging, receipts, or disclosure history is provided for authentication responses.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for detectability/non-repudiation-related gap from the data subject perspective.

title: Authentication service can identify the child through repeated login events
description: Although the child logs in using a parent email and password, the authentication service can associate repeated login attempts with the same account credentials and thereby identify or single out the child/account relationship over time.
assumptions: The service stores or observes account identifiers such as parent email during authentication.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for identification via explicit account identifier in an authentication flow; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Login submissions are linkable across sessions
description: Use of the same parent email for each child login enables the authentication service to link multiple login attempts and sessions to the same household/account, potentially building a profile of the child's usage patterns.
assumptions: The same parent email is reused across sessions and observable by the authentication service.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability based on reuse of a persistent identifier; numbering may differ in some LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Parent email disclosure to parties beyond need-to-know
description: The child login flow transmits a parent's email address to the authentication service. If logged, exposed in diagnostics, or shared internally more broadly than necessary, this reveals personal information about the parent-child relationship and account identity.
assumptions: Authentication requests may be logged or accessible to operators or downstream components.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as generic disclosure of sensitive personal data in transit/processing; exact node id may differ.

title: Password disclosure through insecure handling
description: The password entered in the child login flow is highly sensitive. If the authentication service or supporting infrastructure logs raw credentials, exposes them in traces, or handles them insecurely, confidentiality is compromised.
assumptions: There is some possibility of credential mishandling in application logs, monitoring, crash reports, or support tooling.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for disclosure of authentication secret; exact subtree numbering may vary.

title: Insufficient information about use of parent credentials in child login
description: If the system does not clearly inform users that a parent email and password are used for child authentication, users may not understand what personal data is collected, how it is used, or who can access it.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-context login explanations may be absent or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness style node under non-transparency; exact node id may vary.

title: Child may be unaware that parent account data is being processed
description: A child user may not realize that entering login details involves processing the parent's personal data and ties their activity to the parent's account, reducing meaningful awareness and control.
assumptions: The child is the actor entering credentials and the UX does not provide age-appropriate explanation.
uncertainty_note: This is a best-fit unawareness node; exact numbering may differ between LINDDUN Pro variants.

title: Collection of parent credentials for child access may exceed data minimization expectations
description: Using a parent's email and password as the mechanism for child login may process more personal data than necessary for authenticating a child user, potentially conflicting with data minimization, purpose limitation, or children's privacy requirements.
assumptions: An alternative child-specific or delegated authentication mechanism could have been used.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance is context- and jurisdiction-dependent; node id is an approximate best fit for excessive or inappropriate collection/processing.

title: JWT and child profile payload can enable linking of the child's sessions and profile data
description: If the JWT contains a stable subject identifier, account id, or other persistent claims, the child user or anyone with access to the device can link multiple sessions and received child profiles to the same child account. This creates linkability across uses of the service and potentially across relying contexts if the token is reused or exposed.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT contains stable identifiers or reusable claims rather than pairwise or short-lived opaque references.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id only; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for token-based linkability may vary.

title: JWT claims and child profiles may reveal the child's identity or account attributes
description: The response explicitly includes a JWT marked with userType child and child profiles. If the token or profile data contains name, username, email, date of birth, avatar, account id, or similar attributes, the child can be directly identified on-screen or via local storage, logs, browser history, screenshots, or malware on the endpoint.
assumptions: Assumes profile fields or JWT claims include directly or indirectly identifying attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability/disclosure via response contents.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child-profile data to the endpoint or unintended viewers
description: Returning child profiles to the child user's endpoint exposes potentially sensitive personal data about a minor. If the device is shared, compromised, or used in an unsafe environment, profile data may be observed by parents, siblings, peers, attackers, or other apps. Cached responses or insecure client-side handling can further increase disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes profiles contain personal data beyond a bare opaque identifier and the endpoint may not be fully trusted or private.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a general disclosure node; exact Pro node may differ depending on whether emphasis is on transport, storage, or presentation.

title: JWT leakage can disclose the child's authentication state and embedded claims
description: If the JWT is stored insecurely in local storage, exposed in browser developer tools, intercepted by malicious extensions, or shown in network/error logs, third parties can learn that this child authenticated and may read embedded claims such as role, subject, tenant, or expiry. This is a privacy disclosure even apart from the security risk of token misuse.
assumptions: Assumes client-side storage or logging of the JWT and readable claims in the token payload.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; exact subtree for token disclosure may vary.

title: Over-sharing child profiles in the authentication response
description: The Authentication Service may disclose more profile data than necessary for immediate authentication, such as multiple child profiles, historical metadata, preferences, or internal identifiers. Sending unnecessary fields increases privacy exposure and broadens the audience of personal data at the client.
assumptions: Assumes the flow includes profile attributes not strictly required to complete login.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for excessive disclosure/minimization issue; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Child user may be unaware that profile data and role information are contained in the authentication response
description: A child may not understand that the login response includes a token and profile bundle containing personal information and role designation. This lack of transparency can prevent meaningful awareness of what data is provided to the client and possibly stored there.
assumptions: Assumes the interface does not clearly explain what data is returned, stored, or displayed after authentication.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate for lack of awareness/transparency at the recipient side.

title: Sending child profiles with authentication may exceed consent/minimization expectations for minors
description: Bundling child profiles together with the JWT may process and disclose a minor's personal data beyond what is necessary for authentication, potentially conflicting with consent, purpose limitation, or data minimization obligations. This is especially sensitive because the data concerns a child.
assumptions: Assumes applicable policy or legal requirements require strict minimization and specific justification for profile disclosure to the client.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node only; exact LINDDUN Pro node depends on the compliance framework in scope.

title: Direct identification of the child through submitted identity attributes
description: The flow includes strong identifying data for a child profile: name, date of birth, gender, and government ID. In combination, and especially due to the government ID, the child can be directly identified by the receiving process.
assumptions: P3 stores or otherwise processes the received attributes in identifiable form.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on general LINDDUN Pro knowledge; exact subtree label may vary by catalog version.

title: Linkability of child records across sessions or systems
description: The set of submitted profile attributes, particularly government ID and date of birth, can enable linking this child profile with other records held by the same service or external systems, making separate interactions or datasets correlate to the same child.
assumptions: The attributes are reused, retained, or matched against existing records.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate; exact linkability subtree numbering may differ.

title: Excessive disclosure of sensitive child personal data to the receiving process
description: This flow transfers multiple pieces of sensitive personal data about a minor, including government ID and date of birth. If the receiving process does not strictly need all attributes for profile creation, the flow discloses more personal data than necessary.
assumptions: Not all transmitted fields are strictly necessary for the stated purpose, or access controls/minimization are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id based on generic disclosure/minimization threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Collection without adequate necessity, consent, or legal basis for child data
description: Collecting name, DOB, gender, and especially government ID for a child profile may exceed what is necessary for profile creation or may require explicit parental consent, age-appropriate notices, and a clear legal basis. If those conditions are missing, the collection on this flow is non-compliant.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy imposes data minimization, purpose limitation, and heightened protections for children's data.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-compliance subtree numbering is uncertain and may vary across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Insufficient user awareness about collection and downstream use of child identity data
description: The parent may not fully understand why each field is requested, whether government ID is mandatory, how long the child's data will be retained, and with whom it may be shared. This creates an unawareness threat tied to the collection flow.
assumptions: The interface or notice at collection time does not clearly explain purposes, necessity, retention, and sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact unawareness subtree id may differ.

title: Lack of evidence for valid parental authorization or submission consent
description: Because the flow creates a child profile using sensitive identifying attributes, the system may later be unable to demonstrate that the submission was made or authorized by the parent, or that required consent/approval was properly captured.
assumptions: The system does not bind the submission to auditable proof of parental action or consent records.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related node id is a best estimate from memory.

title: Storing direct child identifiers in profile records
description: The child profile management process may write directly identifying attributes for a child (for example full name, date of birth, account identifiers, or guardian-linked identifiers) into the childprofiles collection, enabling the record to identify a specific child.
assumptions: The profile includes direct or quasi-identifiers rather than only opaque internal references.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identifiability of stored attributes may vary.

title: Profile records may be linkable across sessions, services, or household contexts
description: Persistent child profile entries in the datastore can enable linking of a child's activities, preferences, learning history, or guardian relationships across time and potentially across application features if a stable profile key is reused.
assumptions: The collection uses persistent identifiers or consistent attribute combinations that are reused across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit generic linkability classification.

title: Stored child profiles may reveal sensitive personal attributes
description: The childprofiles collection may contain personal or sensitive information about a child, such as age, developmental data, interests, behavioral information, school-related data, or guardian associations. Unauthorized access or overly broad internal access could disclose these attributes.
assumptions: The stored profile contains personal details beyond a minimal pseudonymous identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic detectability/disclosure-related node under LINDDUN Pro is inferred from memory; exact node may differ.

title: Database contents may allow deduction of additional facts about the child
description: Even if some fields seem innocuous, combinations of profile fields in the collection can permit inference of sensitive facts, such as approximate age, household composition, routines, special needs, or socioeconomic indicators.
assumptions: Multiple profile attributes are stored together and can be queried or analyzed jointly.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit deduction node; exact subtree id may differ.

title: Profile updates may exceed the user's or guardian's consent expectations
description: The process that stores or updates child profiles might persist more information than was clearly consented to by the parent or guardian, or reuse the data for new purposes without obtaining fresh consent.
assumptions: Consent granularity, purpose limitation, or parental authorization checks are incomplete or not enforced before writing to storage.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit generic non-compliance classification.

title: Insufficient evidence of who created or changed a child profile
description: If profile writes and updates are not logged with actor, time, and purpose, it may be impossible to prove whether a parent, administrator, or service component created or modified a child's profile, undermining accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: The flow does not guarantee tamper-evident audit logging for profile changes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-repudiation node.

title: Children or guardians may be unaware of what profile data is stored
description: Once profile data is written to the collection, the existence, scope, retention period, and downstream use of stored child attributes may not be visible to the child or guardian, reducing transparency.
assumptions: The system lacks clear notices, dashboards, or access mechanisms describing stored child profile data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic unawareness node.

title: Search and engagement events can be linked to a child's account or device
description: Video searches, watch requests, likes, and comments sent to the video management service can be correlated over time and tied to the same child account, profile, IP address, cookie, or device identifier, enabling construction of a persistent activity history.
assumptions: The service receives stable identifiers such as account ID, session token, cookie, IP/device metadata, or otherwise can correlate repeated requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability of multiple actions to the same data subject; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary by threat tree version.

title: Identity may be inferred from comments or profile-associated requests
description: Comments and interaction requests may directly contain a username or indirectly reveal identity when combined with account metadata, profile information, contact lists, or distinctive language patterns, making the child identifiable to the service or downstream recipients.
assumptions: Comments or request metadata are associated with account/profile data or are visible to moderators, creators, or other users.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for identifiability from content and metadata; exact subnode may differ across LINDDUN Pro editions.

title: Search, likes, and comments disclose interests and preferences
description: The flow reveals the child's viewing interests, hobbies, sentiments, and possible special-category inferences through search terms, requested videos, liked content, and comment text. This can expose behavioral patterns or sensitive topics.
assumptions: The service stores or analyzes request payloads and engagement history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure of personal information via communicated content and metadata.

title: Metadata disclosure through request context
description: Even where content is limited, timestamps, IP address, device/browser details, language, geolocation hints, and session identifiers in the flow can disclose personal information about the child and their context of use.
assumptions: Standard network/application metadata are logged or observable by the service.
uncertainty_note: Approximate subnode for disclosure via metadata rather than primary content.

title: Actions enable profiling of the child
description: Aggregating searches, requests, likes, and comments allows the service to derive a profile of the child's preferences, habits, likely age range, emotional state, or vulnerabilities, supporting recommendations, targeting, or other automated decisions.
assumptions: The service retains historical interaction data and performs analytics, recommendation, or segmentation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for content/data-driven profiling; exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may differ.

title: Children may not understand how their interactions are collected and used
description: A child user may not be able to meaningfully understand that search queries, video requests, likes, and comments are collected, retained, analyzed, and possibly shared for moderation, recommendation, analytics, or personalization, undermining user unawareness protections.
assumptions: Notices are complex, not child-friendly, or not presented contextually at the time of interaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for insufficient user awareness/transparency; exact subnode may vary.

title: Processing of children's engagement data may exceed lawful or policy limits
description: Collecting and using a child's search terms, viewing requests, likes, and comments for personalization, analytics, retention, or sharing may violate applicable child-privacy requirements or internal minimization/purpose-limitation rules if not strictly necessary and properly governed.
assumptions: The system processes child data and may use it beyond the immediate service request or retain it longer than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with consent, purpose limitation, minimization, or child-specific legal obligations; exact node id may differ.

title: The child may be unable to plausibly deny submitted likes or comments
description: If the system binds likes or comments to the child's account, timestamp, and device/session data, the resulting records can later be used to prove that the child performed the action, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: The service stores logs linking actions to an account or persistent identifier.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-repudiation caused by persistent action logging; numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Stored video metadata and file references may reveal sensitive personal information
description: Persisting video metadata in the videos collection can expose personal data such as uploader identity, timestamps, geolocation, titles, tags, thumbnails, retention markers, or references to underlying video files. If broadly accessible or insufficiently minimized, the datastore enables inference about data subjects and their activities.
assumptions: DS3 stores at least metadata and possibly references or links to associated video file content; access control or minimization may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro information-disclosure subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Cross-record linking of video metadata can enable profiling of individuals
description: Storing multiple video records for the same uploader, viewer context, device, channel, or account in a central collection can allow records to be linked together over time. This may enable profiling of a person's behavior, interests, location patterns, or social relationships.
assumptions: Video records share stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers such as account ids, device ids, IP-derived data, channels, or recurring metadata fields.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; linkability subtree numbering may differ across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Video metadata and associated files may allow identification of data subjects
description: Even if direct identifiers are limited, stored metadata or linked media may contain faces, voices, usernames, exact timestamps, location data, or unique filenames that permit identifying uploaders or recorded individuals.
assumptions: Stored metadata or associated video content contains direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; identifiability may map to a more specific subtree node in some versions.

title: Excessive retention of video metadata or file references can make users detectable over time
description: If the Video Management Service stores metadata and file references longer than necessary, repeated interactions remain observable in the datastore. This can make a user's presence, activity times, and usage patterns detectable across long periods.
assumptions: Retention periods are long or undefined, and records can be queried historically.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; detectability in persistent storage may be represented differently in some LINDDUN Pro trees.

title: Users may be unaware that detailed video metadata and file associations are stored
description: The flow stores or retrieves metadata and associated file information in the backend datastore. If this storage is not transparent to users, they may not understand what attributes are recorded, for how long, and for what secondary purposes they may be used.
assumptions: Notice to users about backend storage, indexing, analytics, or retention is incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; exact unawareness subtree numbering may differ.

title: Storage of video metadata and files may exceed consented purpose or legal basis
description: The service may store metadata or associated file references beyond what users reasonably expect or have consented to, such as extended retention, reuse for analytics, moderation training, profiling, or cross-service sharing. This creates risk of non-compliance with purpose limitation, data minimization, or consent requirements.
assumptions: Processing purposes may extend beyond the primary function of hosting or retrieving videos, or the legal basis may not cover all stored attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; non-compliance subtree structure varies across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Insufficient provenance or audit context for metadata changes can undermine users' ability to challenge actions
description: If updates to video metadata, ownership markers, moderation flags, or deletion state are stored without adequate provenance and audit context, users may be unable to prove what was changed, when, and by whom. This can impair dispute resolution around privacy-impacting actions.
assumptions: The datastore may not preserve trustworthy change history or actor attribution for privacy-relevant modifications.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability is somewhat context-dependent for this flow, and the node id is approximate.

title: Stored search/watch history can reveal sensitive child interests and behaviors
description: Persisting a child's search and watch history in the childprofiles collection creates a risk that anyone with access to the datastore can infer the child's preferences, routines, developmental traits, health-related interests, or other sensitive attributes from the accumulated records.
assumptions: The collection stores fine-grained, user-linked history rather than only short-lived aggregated counters.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for disclosure of sensitive personal data in storage; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: History records enable linkability of multiple child activities over time
description: A persistent child profile that stores search and watch history allows separate actions and sessions to be linked to the same child account or profile, making longitudinal tracking of behavior possible.
assumptions: History entries are associated with a stable child/profile identifier or otherwise retrievable as one profile.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via a stable identifier in stored records; exact subnode may differ.

title: Stored history can identify a child behind otherwise isolated viewing/search events
description: If search and watch events are written into a child profile, events that might otherwise be separate can be tied back to an identifiable child account, increasing identifiability of the child.
assumptions: The profile or collection can be associated with a specific child, household, or account.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for identifiability caused by binding events to a profile.

title: Excessive retention of child history data exceeds necessity
description: Storing detailed search and watch history in the childprofiles collection may retain more personal data, and for longer, than is necessary for the service purpose, especially given the sensitivity of children's data.
assumptions: There is no strict minimization or short retention policy applied before storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization/retention concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may vary.

title: Users may be unaware that child search and watch history is being persisted
description: During profile management, the system may store a child's search and watch history without sufficiently informing the parent or child, reducing awareness of what data is collected and kept.
assumptions: Notice is absent, unclear, or not presented at the point of collection/storage.
uncertainty_note: Approximate best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency at collection and storage.

title: Storing child history may be non-compliant without valid consent or child-specific legal basis
description: Writing a child's detailed search and watch history to persistent storage can violate privacy obligations if parental consent, age-appropriate legal basis, retention limits, or child-specific protections are not properly established.
assumptions: The system is subject to child-data privacy requirements and stores individualized history.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ by taxonomy version.

title: Insufficient proof of notice or consent for history storage can enable repudiation
description: If the profile-management process stores child history without recording when notice was shown or consent/preferences were captured, parties may later dispute whether this storage was authorized or communicated.
assumptions: Authorization, consent, or notice records are not durably logged alongside the storage action.
uncertainty_note: Approximate best-fit node for repudiation related to missing evidence of privacy-relevant actions.

title: Uploader identity exposed through video submission metadata
description: When the parent user uploads a video for approval/rejection, the service can associate the submission with the parent account, device/session identifiers, network metadata, timestamps, and possibly embedded media metadata. This can reveal who submitted specific content and enable identification of the parent user.
assumptions: The upload is authenticated or otherwise tied to an account, session, or network-visible identifier; uploaded media or request metadata may contain identifying information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether identification is modeled via account identity, communication metadata, or media metadata.

title: Video uploads can be linked across submissions and decisions
description: The video management service may correlate multiple uploads, approval/rejection outcomes, timestamps, IP addresses, account identifiers, and content fingerprints to build a profile of the parent user's behavior. This makes separate actions linkable over time.
assumptions: The service stores persistent identifiers, logs, or content fingerprints and retains approval/rejection history.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit generic linkability node; exact subtree depends on whether linkage is through identifiers, metadata, or content-derived fingerprints.

title: Upload transaction and moderation outcome may disclose sensitive information
description: The fact that a parent uploaded a particular video, together with the approval or rejection decision, may disclose sensitive information about the parent or child, such as participation in specific activities, home environment, school events, location clues, or behavioral characteristics visible in the video.
assumptions: Video content or moderation outcome is accessible to internal staff, logs, downstream systems, or unauthorized parties beyond what is strictly necessary.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; disclosure may stem from both content and metadata, and the precise subtree depends on the disclosure channel.

title: Embedded metadata in uploaded videos may reveal hidden personal data
description: Uploaded video files can contain EXIF/container metadata such as creation time, device model, geolocation, or editing history. If the service ingests, stores, or exposes this metadata during approval/rejection processing, additional personal data may be disclosed beyond the visible video itself.
assumptions: The upload pipeline preserves or logs file/container metadata and does not strip sensitive fields before storage or review.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may belong to a more specific disclosure-via-metadata subtree in LINDDUN Pro; using a general disclosure node as best estimate.

title: Insufficient transparency about approval/rejection processing and data use
description: The parent user may not understand what data from the upload is collected, how the video is reviewed, whether automated checks are used, who can access the video, how long the video and decision are retained, or why a rejection occurred. This creates unawareness about privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices, upload UI, or rejection messaging do not fully explain processing, retention, reviewers, or decision logic.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic unawareness node; exact subtree depends on whether the gap concerns collection, retention, sharing, or decision logic transparency.

title: Upload and moderation processing may exceed consent or stated purpose
description: Videos submitted for approval/rejection may be further used for analytics, model training, staff quality review, policy enforcement beyond the original purpose, or retained longer than expected. If such uses are not covered by valid consent or another lawful basis, the flow creates non-compliance risk.
assumptions: The service reuses uploaded content or moderation results beyond the immediate approval/rejection purpose, or consent/lawful basis is not clearly established.
uncertainty_note: General non-compliance node chosen as best estimate; exact subtree depends on the specific legal basis, consent, purpose limitation, and retention obligations in scope.

title: Parent user may be unable to prove or contest submission and moderation events
description: If the service lacks adequate, user-accessible evidence of what was uploaded, when it was submitted, and why it was approved or rejected, the parent may not be able to demonstrate their actions or challenge an incorrect moderation outcome. Conversely, the service may also be unable to prove what the parent actually submitted if logging is weak.
assumptions: There is no reliable receipt, audit trail, hash, timestamp, or explanation associated with the upload and moderation decision.
uncertainty_note: Mapping to repudiation is somewhat context-dependent in privacy threat modeling; included because disputes over submission and decision history are plausible for this flow.

title: Exposure of child's video-viewing behavior to the service provider
description: Streaming approved video to the child reveals that the child device is online and which approved content is being delivered at a given time. This can disclose the child's viewing habits, interests, and activity patterns to the Video Management Service or associated operators beyond what is necessary for simple delivery.
assumptions: The streaming flow or surrounding telemetry allows the service to observe which video is sent and when it is consumed.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labeling for content-consumption disclosure may vary.

title: Linkability of multiple viewing sessions for the same child
description: Repeated streaming sessions from the Video Management Service to the child can be linked together via persistent identifiers, session tokens, device identifiers, or network metadata, enabling construction of a profile of the child's media consumption over time.
assumptions: The flow uses stable identifiers or otherwise observable metadata that persist across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact subnode may differ.

title: Identifiability of the child through streaming metadata
description: Even if the video payload itself is approved content, associated metadata such as account identifiers, device IDs, IP address, or personalized stream URLs can make the child identifiable to the service or intermediaries handling the flow.
assumptions: The stream request/response context contains user-, device-, or account-specific metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct or indirect identifiability from metadata.

title: Unawareness of tracking or personalization in video streaming
description: The child may be unaware that video streaming can involve logging of viewing events, quality metrics, timestamps, and other behavioral data, or that the delivered content may be selected or adapted based on prior behavior or parental settings.
assumptions: The system collects streaming telemetry or applies personalized/filtered delivery logic not clearly explained to the child.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro node for user unawareness about monitoring/transparency may vary.

title: Streaming data processed beyond necessity or lawful basis
description: The video streaming flow may involve collection or retention of more personal data than needed for delivery, such as detailed viewing logs or device metadata, or may lack child-appropriate transparency, consent/authorization, or retention controls required by applicable privacy obligations.
assumptions: The implementation stores or reuses streaming-related personal data beyond immediate content delivery.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit compliance node; specific LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ depending on the obligation considered.

title: Excessive detectability of child presence or activity from streaming traffic
description: Observers who can see the flow may detect when the child is present, active, and consuming video based on the existence, timing, volume, or frequency of the stream, even without accessing the video content itself.
assumptions: Network observers or service-side analysts can observe traffic patterns or stream initiation events.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability from traffic existence/patterns rather than content disclosure.

title: Linkability of child browsing history across sessions and contexts
description: The childprofiles collection can provide persistent identifiers or stable profile attributes together with browsing data to the AI Recommendation Engine, enabling the engine to link a child's actions across time, devices, or contexts and build a consolidated behavioral profile.
assumptions: Assumes records in childprofiles include stable account, device, household, or profile identifiers, or combinations of attributes that act as quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode wording may differ.

title: Identifiability of a child from profile and browsing attributes
description: Browsing data combined with profile fields in the MongoDB collection may directly or indirectly identify a specific child when sent to the AI engine, especially if the dataset includes names, account IDs, device IDs, age bands, school-related interests, location patterns, or rare behavior combinations.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may include direct identifiers or sufficiently unique quasi-identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from direct or indirect identifiers; exact subnode numbering may vary.

title: Excessive disclosure of detailed child browsing behavior to the AI engine
description: The planned flow may disclose more child browsing information to the AI Recommendation Engine than is necessary for generating recommendations, such as full histories, timestamps, inferred interests, or sensitive browsing categories, increasing privacy exposure within the receiving process.
assumptions: Assumes data minimization controls and field-level filtering are not yet fully defined because the flow is marked planned.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for unnecessary disclosure / over-collection by the receiving process; exact LINDDUN Pro node label may differ.

title: Unawareness of child-profile use for AI-driven recommendation
description: Data subjects or their guardians may be unaware that browsing data stored in childprofiles is repurposed and analyzed by the AI Recommendation Engine to infer preferences or drive personalization, especially if this use is newly planned and not transparently communicated.
assumptions: Assumes notices, consent flows, or age-appropriate explanations for this planned processing are incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/transparency about downstream processing; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Processing child browsing data for AI recommendations without a valid lawful basis or purpose limitation
description: Using child browsing data from childprofiles for AI recommendations may be incompatible with the original collection purpose, exceed user or guardian expectations, or lack an appropriate lawful basis and age-appropriate safeguards, creating non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the original purpose of collection may not have explicitly included AI personalization for children and that special child-data obligations apply.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for purpose limitation/lawful basis non-compliance; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode id is uncertain.

title: Inference of sensitive traits about a child from browsing data
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may derive sensitive or special-category inferences from browsing patterns, such as health concerns, emotional state, religion, political leaning, or vulnerabilities, leading to disclosure of information that was not explicitly collected but becomes available through analysis.
assumptions: Assumes model features or outputs can infer latent traits from behavioral signals.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure through inference/profiling; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Disclosure of personal browsing data to third-party advertisers
description: The planned flow sends browsing data from the AI Recommendation Engine to external advertisers. Browsing histories, viewed items, clicks, searches, and inferred interests can reveal personal behavior and preferences. Disclosure to third parties increases the chance of unauthorized or unexpected access and secondary use.
assumptions: Assumes the browsing data contains or can be linked to user-level behavioral information rather than only fully aggregated anonymous statistics.
uncertainty_note: Tree node given at a generic disclosure level because the exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node depends on whether the data is raw, pseudonymous, aggregated, or enriched with identifiers.

title: Linkability of browsing behavior across contexts by advertisers
description: Advertisers receiving browsing data may combine it with their own identifiers, cookies, device fingerprints, campaign logs, or brokered datasets to link a user's activity across services, sessions, or devices. This can enable persistent cross-context profiles.
assumptions: Assumes advertisers have other datasets or identifiers enabling record linkage.
uncertainty_note: Using a generic linkability node; a more specific node would depend on whether direct identifiers, stable pseudonyms, or quasi-identifiers are included in the flow.

title: Identifiability of individuals from shared browsing data
description: Even if explicit identifiers are omitted, advertisers may identify individuals by combining browsing patterns, timestamps, device data, location hints, or account-level campaign data with auxiliary information. Rich behavioral data is often highly identifying.
assumptions: Assumes the shared browsing data includes enough granularity for re-identification or is accompanied by metadata useful for matching.
uncertainty_note: Generic identifiability node selected because exact sub-node depends on the specific attributes included in the payload.

title: Use of browsing data beyond user expectations
description: Users may expect browsing data to be used for recommendations inside the service, not to be transferred to external advertisers for ad targeting, profiling, measurement, or resale. This creates a risk that processing purposes are not transparent or aligned with user expectations.
assumptions: Assumes users were not clearly informed about this planned advertiser sharing and did not reasonably expect it.
uncertainty_note: Mapped to a generic unawareness node because the exact sub-node depends on the notice/consent design and transparency controls.

title: Potential non-compliance from third-party advertising use of browsing data
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may violate purpose limitation, data minimization, consent, transparency, retention, or cross-border transfer requirements if not properly governed. The external recipient may also process the data in ways inconsistent with declared purposes or applicable law.
assumptions: Assumes the organization is subject to privacy obligations requiring a lawful basis, appropriate notices, and controls on onward transfers.
uncertainty_note: Generic non-compliance node used; exact sub-node depends on the applicable regulatory regime and contractual/data-governance controls.

title: Detectability of user interests or sensitive traits from advertiser-bound data
description: Browsing data sent to advertisers may make it easy to detect that a user is associated with certain products, topics, or categories. Even without full identification, observers or recipients may detect the presence of sensitive interests such as health, politics, religion, sexuality, or financial distress from the transferred signals.
assumptions: Assumes the browsing data includes category-level or event-level information from which notable interests can be inferred.
uncertainty_note: Generic detectability node selected because the exact LINDDUN Pro branch may depend on whether the focus is detectability of communication, attributes, or sensitive-category membership.

title: Stored government ID images enable direct identification
description: Government ID images typically contain name, photo, document number, date of birth, and other unique identifiers. Storing these images in the file system creates a strong ability to directly identify the data subject from the stored content if accessed or processed.
assumptions: The uploaded files contain full or partially legible government-issued identity documents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for direct identifiability from data content; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Government ID images can link user accounts to real-world identities
description: Persisting ID images alongside authentication-related context can link a user's account or session to their real-world civil identity, enabling correlation across records, services, or events.
assumptions: The file path, metadata, or surrounding application context associates each stored image with a specific account or authentication event.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via stored identifiers and context.

title: Sensitive personal attributes are disclosed through stored ID images
description: Government ID images reveal extensive personal data such as legal name, address, date of birth, nationality, sex marker, photo, and document number. Unauthorized access to the stored files would disclose highly sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Stored images are accessible to administrators, services, backups, or attackers beyond strictly authorized personnel.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure from stored personal data; exact numbering may differ.

title: Storing raw government ID images may exceed necessity or legal basis
description: Persisting full-resolution government ID images in backend/uploads may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, storage limitation, or other compliance obligations if only limited attributes or temporary verification are necessary.
assumptions: The system may not strictly require long-term storage of full ID images after verification, or retention/consent/legal-basis controls may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to unnecessary retention/over-collection; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Users may be unaware that ID images are stored in backend file storage
description: If the service does not clearly inform users that their government ID images are persisted in backend/uploads, for how long, and for what purposes, users may not have adequate awareness of the collection and storage practice.
assumptions: Privacy notices or upload UI may not clearly describe storage location, retention, access, and downstream use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient awareness/transparency; numbering may differ.

title: Stored ID images may be used beyond the original authentication purpose
description: Once retained in the file system, government ID images could be repurposed for analytics, fraud modeling, employee review, law-enforcement response, or other secondary uses that data subjects did not expect or approve.
assumptions: Purpose binding and downstream-use restrictions are not technically or organizationally enforced.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for policy/processing unawareness or secondary use under detectability/content exposure themes; exact LINDDUN Pro mapping may vary.

title: JWT in localStorage can reveal account identity and session claims to scripts with browser access
description: Storing a JWT in browser localStorage exposes its contents to any script executing in the page origin, including injected third-party or malicious scripts. If the token contains subject identifiers, email, roles, tenant IDs, or other claims, those claims can reveal the user's identity or account associations beyond what is necessary for the immediate interaction.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT is not encrypted and contains readable identity or profile claims, which is common for bearer JWTs.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for information disclosure of stored sensitive data; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: Persistent JWT enables cross-session and repeated linking of the same browser user
description: A JWT stored in localStorage can persist across browser sessions until explicitly removed. A stable token or stable subject claim allows actions performed over time from the same browser profile to be linked together, enabling tracking of the same user across visits and potentially across app areas sharing the same origin.
assumptions: Assumes token lifetime or refresh behavior causes persistence long enough to correlate multiple visits or transactions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via persistent identifiers in client storage; exact subtree id may vary.

title: JWT contents in localStorage may expose user-related attributes to unauthorized observers
description: If the JWT carries personal data or inferable attributes, storage in localStorage makes those attributes available to any party with access to the browser context for that origin. This can disclose profile details, authorization scopes, organizational membership, or other personal characteristics to entities not intended to learn them.
assumptions: Assumes local browser access by scripts, extensions, shared-device users, or forensic access, and that the token includes or implies personal attributes.
uncertainty_note: This is a disclosure threat distinct from direct identification because claims may reveal attributes even without a full identity. Node id is approximate.

title: Client-side persistent storage of authentication token may exceed user expectations or consent
description: Users may not expect an authentication token to be persistently stored in localStorage, especially if this enables long-lived sessions, tracking across visits, or access by client-side scripts. If retention period, purpose, or exposure are not transparently communicated and controlled, the storage can conflict with user consent, data minimization, or storage-limitation expectations.
assumptions: Assumes the application does not clearly communicate token storage behavior or offer meaningful controls over persistence.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends strongly on jurisdiction, notices, consent model, and whether the JWT contains personal data; node id is best-effort.

title: Excessive disclosure of child history to parent
description: The flow sends child history from Child Profile Management to the parent for review. If the response contains more history than is necessary for the specific review purpose, sensitive details about the child may be disclosed unnecessarily to the parent.
assumptions: Assumes the child history may include sensitive events, behavioral data, health/education-related notes, or longitudinal records, and that purpose-based minimization is not strictly enforced.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected for unauthorized or unnecessary disclosure on a data flow; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode may differ.

title: Child record becomes identifiable to the receiving parent
description: The child history in this flow is inherently tied to a specific child and parent relationship. If identifiers are included directly, or if the history content is distinctive enough, the child can be identified within the dataset and across interactions, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted history includes direct identifiers or highly specific contextual details.
uncertainty_note: Identifiability is inherent in many parent-child account contexts; node id is a best-fit approximation.

title: Linkability of events across the child's timeline
description: Providing a consolidated child history allows the parent to link multiple events, activities, and records over time into a richer profile of the child. This may enable inferences beyond the original purpose of individual records.
assumptions: Assumes the history aggregates multiple records over time rather than a single isolated event.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit linkability node for correlating multiple records within a history view; exact subnode may vary.

title: Insufficient transparency about what child history is shared
description: The parent may receive child history without the child or parent being clearly informed which categories of data, time periods, or inferred information are included. Lack of transparency can prevent understanding of the privacy impact of the disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes notices or UI explanations for the history retrieval may be incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness often depends on surrounding notice and interface design, which are not described here.

title: Sharing child history without a valid legal basis or policy authorization
description: The system may disclose child history to a parent in situations where consent, guardianship status, age-related rules, custody restrictions, or applicable child-privacy regulations do not permit access. This creates non-compliance risk for the disclosure flow.
assumptions: Assumes access-control and policy checks may not fully account for legal guardianship, custody, age thresholds, or jurisdiction-specific requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node chosen broadly for missing legal/policy basis; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Disclosure to the wrong parent or guardian account
description: If the parent user receiving the flow is misbound, has stale authorization, or shares credentials with others, child history could be disclosed to an unauthorized recipient. The privacy harm is concentrated at the receiving external entity side of the flow.
assumptions: Assumes account binding, session integrity, or guardianship validation may fail or become outdated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for unauthorized recipient exposure; exact subnode may vary.
